properties.areaDesc: Far Northwest Highlands; Northwest Highlands; West Central Mountains; West Central Highlands; Jemez Mountains
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 23 at 4:59AM MDT until October 24 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of north central and west central New Mexico,
including the following areas, in north central New Mexico, Far
Northwest Highlands, Jemez Mountains and Northwest Highlands. In
west central New Mexico, West Central Highlands and West Central
Mountains.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Scattered-to-numerous showers and thunderstorms will continue
today and this evening. Some of today's stronger storms will be
capable of producing rain at rates up to 1 inch per hour. Some
locations will receive repeated rounds of storms with over 1.5
inches of additional rain accumulation possible. Locations where
the ground is saturated from heavy rain that fell on Thursday
will be favored for rapid runoff and flash flooding, even from
only moderate rainfall today.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low lying areas due to tidal flooding.

* WHERE...Shoreline in Saint Mary's County.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM EDT this afternoon, especially around the
time of high tide.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, water covers roads on Saint George
Island, is in yards, and is approaching structures. To the east,
inundation is occurring at multiple marinas off Saint Mary's
River, Smith Creek, and Jutland Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tides one and a half to two feet above
normal. The next high tide at Point Lookout is at 11:55 AM. The
next high tide at Piney Point is at 12:49 PM. The next high tide
at Coltons Point is at 1:25 PM.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Gale Warning issued October 23 at 3:05AM PDT until October 23 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...North winds 25 to 30 kt with gusts up to 40 kt and seas
10 to 12 feet.

* WHERE...Waters from Cape Mendocino to Pt. Arena CA from 10 to
60 nm.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
properties.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for severe conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Very steep and hazardous north winds 10 to 20 kt with
gusts up to 35 kt expected.

* WHERE...Humboldt Bay.

* WHEN...From 9 AM this morning to 9 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Very steep and hazardous seas could capsize or cause
damage to vessels.
